items.title: 🚨 BREAKING: Hackers are hitting supermarket freezers in 5 countries at the same time.
items.summary:
🚨 BREAKING: Hackers are hitting supermarket freezers in 5 countries at the same time.

This is what Covid looked like in week 1. A few countries. Small numbers. Nobody called it a crisis.

1/ Sweden: stores say hackers hit their cooling overnight. One says fridges and freezers were set to 50°C, and the food spoiled. ICA Kvantum stores in Sjöbo and Tomelilla were hit, plus at least 6 Coop stores. Sjöbo stayed closed through the morning, threw out all affected goods and apologized. ICA says it is working to restore normal operations. In Sankt Olof a store manager said "everything is ruined." Sweden's National Cybersecurity Centre is working on several incidents.

2/ Estonia: the CEO of cooling firm Kitman Coldtech says several clients were targeted and a large chain's freezer was raised to +50°C. It was found and addressed in about 10 minutes, no major damage.

3/ Ireland: SuperValu pulled ALL fresh and frozen food from 13 stores. Its owner, Musgrave, confirmed a "cybersecurity incident" on a "specific model" of fridge.

4/ Luxembourg: Ahold Delhaize says an "IT incident" hit fridges and freezers at dozens of its supermarkets across Luxembourg and Belgium.

5/ Belgium: more than 40 Delhaize, at least 15 Carrefour and around 5 Spar stores were hit. Cold storage climbed to 15°C. Aisles were closed off and large amounts of stock were destroyed. A notice at one Proxy Delhaize said its systems had "fallen victim to hacking."

Now zoom out.

A freezer normally sits at -18°C. In Estonia, hackers reportedly got in through older controllers. In France, the controller maker said many devices were obsolete or ran outdated firmware. Raise the temperature overnight and the food rots. "You can't unspoil food," one professor said.

It did not start today. 3 weeks ago hackers raised freezers at more than 350 sites in France to as high as 50°C. There were fires. Intermarché's CEO put the cost at "tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day." Sources suspect Russian involvement there. No group has claimed it. That same day an analyst said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium were affected too.

Covid emptied the shelves. Nobody is calling this a crisis yet. But the Financial Times already puts the ruined food at millions of euros.

Officials say the Pentagon is treating late-August freezer failures on US military bases as a suspected hack. At least 6 base stores were hit. Army investigators are working with French law enforcement.

5 countries in one day. 11 countries named since August.

Share this. Everyone should know about it.

results.input: Không cần tra cứu: giải thích ngắn gọn sự khác nhau giữa dữ liệu có cấu trúc và dữ liệu phi cấu trúc.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là sự khác biệt chính giữa **Dữ liệu có cấu trúc** và **Dữ liệu phi cấu trúc**:

### 1. Dữ liệu có cấu trúc (Structured Data)
* **Định dạng:** Đã được định nghĩa sẵn, có khuôn dạng rõ ràng (theo hàng và cột).
* **Lưu trữ:** Trong các cơ sở dữ liệu quan hệ (RDBMS) như SQL (MySQL, PostgreSQL), bảng Excel, CSV.
* **Dễ xử lý:** Dễ truy vấn, tìm kiếm và phân tích bằng các câu lệnh tiêu chuẩn (ví dụ: SQL).
* **Ví dụ:** Số điện thoại, ngày sinh, mã giao dịch ngân hàng, mã định danh (ID).

---

### 2. Dữ liệu phi cấu trúc (Unstructured Data)
* **Định dạng:** Không có cấu trúc cố định hay mô hình dữ liệu định sẵn.
* **Lưu trữ:** Lưu dưới dạng tệp tin, Data Lake, hệ thống NoSQL.
* **Khó xử lý:** Cần các công cụ nâng cao như trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI), xử lý ngôn ngữ tự nhiên (NLP) hoặc thị giác máy tính để phân tích và trích xuất thông tin.
* **Ví dụ:** Văn bản (email, tài liệu Word), hình ảnh, video, tệp âm thanh, bài viết trên mạng xã hội.

---

**Tóm lại:** Dữ liệu có cấu trúc giống như một bảng Excel được sắp xếp ngăn nắp, còn dữ liệu phi cấu trúc giống như một tập hợp tài liệu gồm văn bản, hình ảnh và video chưa qua sắp xếp.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence & Next-Gen Breeding
items.summary:
Artificial Intelligence & Next-Gen Breeding

Accelerated Delivery: Traditional crop variety development is being cut nearly in half, shrinking from 6 to 7 years down to just 3 to 4 years.

Key Technology Pillars
1. Breeding Accelerators & Biobreeding: 
Scientists use AI computing and high-density genome sequencing to run "seed entrance exams." They screen DNA for specific molecular markers early on, ensuring only top-performing seeds are multiplied.

2. Genetics-by-Environment (GxE) Modeling: Companies like Lidea deploy machine learning to analyze how a seed's transcriptomic data interacts with environmental variables (soil, water, temperature). This predicts and maximizes crop success for specific planting locations.

3. Quantum Computing Design: 
Agtech leaders like Syngenta use quantum computing to simulate complex cellular behaviors and stress responses at a molecular level, designing vegetable seeds before field trials begin.

Renewable energy brings many benefits for the EU. It’s clean, sustainable, cheap to produce and homegrown – giving a boost to Europe’s energy independence. It also offers benefits for the local communities where Europe’s renewable energy projects are located. [...] A renewable energy project in the area can also reduce local consumers’ reliance on imported fossil fuels, and the pollution that comes with it, including to the local environment. Designing nature-friendly projects, projects that allow multiple uses of space and projects that combine different technologies, can maximise benefits for communities.

## Public engagement matters [...] The roll-out of renewables in Europe is accelerating. The numbers speak for themselves: from 12.5% in 2010, the share of renewable energy sources in EU energy consumption has been steadily increasing, reaching 26.2% in 2025. Building on this trend, yet acknowledging that further structural progress is needed, in 2023, the EU revised its renewable energy target of 32% by 2030 upwards. Collectively, we want to reach at least 42.5% of energy from renewable sources in the EU’s gross final energy

items.title: Countries leading the charge on renewable energy - Climate Council
items.summary: The need for a switch to renewable energy is more urgent than ever. Climate change, driven by the extraction and burning of coal, oil and gas, is already wreaking havoc on communities, economies and ecosystems right around the world. The easiest, quickest and most effective way of driving down climate pollution and giving ourselves the best chance of kicking climate change’s butt is by moving to an energy system based on renewables and storage. [...] Getting fossil fuels out of homes, businesses and transport, and instead powering ourselves with renewable energy, can also provide real, lasting protection from overseas energy shocks that the world is now experiencing for the second time in just four years. The sun and wind are free, abundant energy sources that can’t be embargoed, blockaded or weaponised. [...] Here in Australia, we are building out renewable power and storage at record rates, and they now make up 40% of our electricity across the country (and 45% of our main grid which covers NSW, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia and Tasmania). We are far from alone in the global renewable rollout: in the first half of 2025, for the first time ever, the world made more power with renewables than from coal. In total, almost 100 countries now make more than 35% of their power with renewables.

items.title: Ask the expert: What to know about renewable energy in Michigan
items.summary: When renewable energy is proposed on farmland, it’s important to consider opportunities for dual use. Farming can generally continue around wind turbines, and solar projects can accommodate activities such as sheep grazing or certain crops. Renewable energy also is only one reason farmland leaves production; residential and commercial development and changing agricultural economics also play a role.

Abstract
The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or
convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best
performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention
mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer,
based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions
entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to
be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly
less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-
to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including
ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task,
our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after
training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the
best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to
other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with
large and limited training data.
∗Equal contribution. Listing order is random. Jakob proposed replacing RNNs with self-attention and started
the effort to evaluate this idea. Ashish, with Illia, designed and implemented the first Transformer models and
has been crucially involved in every aspect of this work. Noam proposed scaled dot-product attention, multi-head
attention and the parameter-free position representation and became the other person involved in nearly every
detail. Niki designed, implemented, tuned and evaluated countless model variants in our original codebase and
tensor2tensor. Llion also experimented with novel model variants, was responsible for our initial codebase, and
efficient inference and visualizations. Lukasz and Aidan spent countless long days designing various parts of and
implementing tensor2tensor, replacing our earlier codebase, greatly improving results and massively accelerating
our research.
